summary: Every valid result contains exactly 2^n integers, so merely materializing the required output takes exponential time. The current direct Gray transform computes each output once and matches that bound.

optimality.argument: The contract requires a list containing all 2^n distinct n-bit values, so any implementation must create 2^n output entries and takes Omega(2^n) time in the output model. The current list comprehension iterates over exactly those 2^n ranks and performs one shift and one XOR per rank, giving O(2^n) time. Excluding the required returned list, it keeps only constant scalar state.

replacement_checks.evidence: A valid Gray-code sequence has exactly 2^n entries by contract, and each entry must be materialized in the returned list.
The range has exactly 2^n values, and the comprehension applies a constant-time shift and XOR to each value once.

The source-fidelity-verified examples cover the complete two-bit cycle and the minimum legal bit width; black-box real-test execution validates the existing semantic Gray-code checks without inspecting their definitions.
